previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, mechanical mitral valve on warfarin, type 1 diabetes with functioning pancreatic transplants, and heart failure was admitted for dizziness and new-onset chest pain. She associated the dizziness with recent initiation of pregabalin, which she discontinued prior to admission. Her symptoms were complicated by supratherapeutic INR (3.8), mild hyperkalemia, and pulmonary edema. Chest pain developed during transfer and resolved with tramadol; serial troponins were mildly elevated but stable, without evidence of acute ischemia. She underwent two hemodialysis sessions, which improved fluid status, potassium, and overall symptoms. Warfarin was held and restarted at home dose, with bridging anticoagulation using enoxaparin. Dizziness resolved, and pregabalin was discontinued due to suspected side effects. She was discharged home with services, asymptomatic, on her baseline medications plus short-term Lovenox.

further evaluation.

as follows: 98.3, 136/83, 84, 18, 100% RA. Labs were notable for 
Hgb/Hct of 6.2/20.4, platelets of 136, INR of 10.6, K of 5.4, 
and Cr of 7.2. She receieved a lidocaine patch, tacrolimus 2mg, 
and temazepam 30mg, as well as 1 units of packed red blood cells 
and 1 unit of FFP; she declined vitamin K, having found it to 
lower her INR excessively in the past. Vital signs at transfer 
were as follows: 97.7, 129/59, 82, 18, 97% RA. She reportedly 
experienced transient substernal chest pain in the ambulance, 
resolved with SL nitroglycerin x1.  
On the floor, she describes ongoing malaise, experienced in the 
context of similar such episodes in the past, but is otherwise 
without complaint on the floor. She denies falls, dysarthria, 
facial droop, or focal weakness. She does endorse intermittent 
mild nonradiating substernal chest pain at rest for the past few 
days coinciding with low hematocrit without associated 
diaphoresis or shortness of breath; she recalls that chest pain 
has occurred in the context of similar such episodes in the past 
and is milder than her true anginal equivalent. She denies 
melena, bright red blood per rectum, or excessive bleeding from 
any orifice. She last took warfarin 3 days prior to admission.

PATIENT:
Mrs. ___ is a ___ with history of failed renal transplant x2

ACUTE ISSUES: 
# Supratherapeutic INR in setting of MVR: 
INR supratherapeutic to 10.6 at OSH. Was given one unit FFP but 
declined vitamin K.  Transfereed to ___ for further 
management, INR on arrival was 4.3. Warfarin was continued even 
while patient was supratherapeutic given history of rapid 
development of subtherapeutic values. Warfarin restarted at 
lower dose (5mg to 2.5mg) and INR trended daily. While 
hospitalized her INR downtrended to a trough of 2.3 (therapuetic 
target 3.0-3.5) despite ongoing warfarin therapy. Heparin drip 
bridge started when INR subtherapuetic and discontinued the next 
day when INR rebounded to therapuetic range. The next day, INR 
was supratherapeutic and lower dose of warfarin was continued 
through discharge.

# Acute-on-chronic anemia: 
Hct was 20.4 at OSH, down from 29 at previous discharge 1.5 
weeks ago.  Received 1 unit of PRBCs and transfered to ___. 
Upon arrival, was given another unit of PRBCs for ongoing chest 
pain (see below). Admission exam notable for guiac positive 
stool, consistent with previously diagnosed lower GI bleed. Iron 
panels and reticulocyte index notable for anemia of chronic 
disease and underproduction. Hemolysis labs also suggestive of 
ongoing RBC destruction. During hospitalization patient received 
an additional unit of PRBCs with both of her dialysis sessions. 
Hematocrit downtrended after first session of HD, but stabilized 
after the second.
Discharged with hematocrit of 24.2.

# Chest Pain: 
Patient presented with intermittent chest pain two days prior to 
presentation and on hospital day 1 that was relieved with 
sublingual nitroglycerin. Suspected to be due to demand ischemia 
from anemia/low O2 carrying capacity. EKG not concerning for 
ischemia but patient noted to have mild troponin leak. Chest 
pain resolved after initial ___ transfusion and did not 
reoccur during hospitalization. 

# Anion gap metabolic acidosis: Anion gap on admission thought 
to be due to ESRD.  Addressed through regularly scheduled 
hemodialysis

# Elevated alkaline phosphatase: Alkaline phosphatase was 
elevated to to 112 on admission, down from prior on recent 
admission.  No other LFT abnormalities observed.

pancreatic transplant: Home diabetes regimen continued while 
inpatient
# Thrombocytopenia: Platelet count at her baseline in 120s on

# Chronic hand pain: Continued lidocaine patches.  
# HFdEF: No decompensation while inpatient.  
# Vitamin D deficiency: Continued home cholecalciferol.  
# GERD: Held home omeprazole in favor of pantoprazole IV,
